brief.scope:
The fixture batch (four fixture apps, `ops/bin/fixture.sh`, the findings lever) had its one fix round (two implement runs) and its security re-audit returned changes again. By D-LADDER-1 the batch gets no second fix round; the unresolved findings are this slice's scope and it runs the whole ladder: tests (Grok) → skeptic → implement (Codex) per S bucket → audits once → one fix round → security re-audit → draft PR.
D-LADDER-1 (register, standing ratified, `ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json`, decided_by owner 2026-09-04): an implement run covers at most one S bucket and an M slice is implemented in two runs the plan names; the security and adversarial audits run once per batch on the merged tree, never per slice, with one fix round and the security re-audit only; the skeptic runs once on the first tests and never on the fixed tests.
Bucket sizes (owner, 2026-09-04): S = 1–3 files, one implement run under 10 minutes; M = two named S buckets (run A, run B), each landed and green alone; L = split.

findings.claim: The test plants the non-allowlisted probe `./probes/does-not-exist-syn` but requires UNREACHABLE and exit 1. The contract requires every unmatched probe string to refuse class `probe`, so a correct implementation cannot make this test green.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_lever.py").read_text(); b=s[s.index("def test_prove_spawn_failure_is_unreachable_never_a_colour"):s.index("def test_prove_timeout_is_unreachable_never_a_colour")]; assert "./probes/does-not-exist-syn" in b and "UNREACHABLE" in b and "assert_refusal" not in b'

findings.claim: Every new assertion observes one Codex implement launch after `launch_ok()` returns, and none requires `<job>/scratch/git/`. A launcher that applies isolation only to Codex writes, creates directories after child exit, and omits `scratch/git/` passes while violating the all-children, before-spawn contract.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_isolation.py").read_text(); b=s[s.index("class JobDirectoryScratchIsTheChildTmp"):]; assert "job=\"implement\", harness=\"codex\", stage=\"code\"" in b and "harness=\"claude\"" not in b and "harness=\"grok\"" not in b and "scratch / \"git\"" not in b'

findings.claim: The tests remove HOME and several named secrets and reject one semicolon-bearing probe, but never require the exact environment key set or reject extra argv on an otherwise valid form. A blacklist parser accepting `sh probes/syn-01.sh extra`, retaining `shell=True`, and forwarding unplanted ambient keys survives.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_lever.py").read_text(); g=s[s.index("def test_prove_refuses_an_off_list_probe"):s.index("def test_prove_refuses_a_probe_script_symlink")]; e=s[s.index("def test_prove_scrubs_ambient_secrets"):s.index("def test_prove_fixed_does_not_write")]; assert "true; echo" in g and "sh probes/syn-01.sh extra" not in s and "self.assertEqual(keys" not in e'

findings.claim: Both containment plants make the leaf itself a symlink. An implementation rejecting only `path.is_symlink()` passes while a regular leaf reached through a symlinked parent still escapes `probes/` or the fixture; the contract requires containment of the fully resolved path.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_lever.py").read_text(); b=s[s.index("def test_prove_refuses_a_probe_script_symlink"):s.index("def test_prove_fixed_does_not_copy_ignored_vendor")]; assert "escape.symlink_to(outside)" in b and "original.symlink_to(outside)" in b and "parent-symlink" not in b and "linkdir" not in b'

findings.claim: The ignored-vendor test re-reads the supplied tree after `prove`; it never observes the trial or gives copied bytes a side effect. An implementation can retain conditional copying of ignored `vendor/`, then emit the expected toolchain refusal, and pass despite admitting untracked bytes into the trial.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_lever.py").read_text(); b=s[s.index("def test_prove_fixed_does_not_copy_ignored_vendor"):s.index("def test_prove_fixed_refuses_toolchain_when_a_fault_names_vendor")]; assert "self.assert_refusal(proc, \"toolchain\")" in b and "vendor_bin.read_bytes()" in b and "trial" not in b and "PWNED" not in b'

findings.claim: The lever-facing validator test covers only a missing `lineage`; the separate helper test invokes `record.validate()` without coupling it to `grade`. A grader that manually rejects missing lineage and the tested statuses but never calls `record.validate` passes while accepting other invalid record shapes.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_grade.py").read_text(); b=s[s.index("def test_grade_refuses_a_record_that_fails_record_validate"):s.index("def test_grade_refuses_record_when_the_job_is_not_a_review_job")]; assert "del payload[\"lineage\"]" in b and "mod.validate" not in b and "RecordError" not in b'

envelope.note: Reviewed only contracts and tests; no implementation was read. The test guard reported all plants guarded. The supplied red-run artifact was read, but local reruns could not reach assertions because the read-only sandbox provided no writable temporary directory.
